Formosa Advanced Technologies.why: Memory back-end OEM: packages and tests DRAM ICs and assembles memory modules, mainly for Nanya Technology (71% of 2025 net sales); AI-driven DRAM tightness (HBM/DDR5 crowding out DDR4) is lifting its packaging/test volumes, OEM prices and capex (TSV, bumping, chip stacking at its new Factory 5).
Formosa Advanced Technologies.evidence: Formosa Advanced Technologies 2025 annual report: customers above 10% of sales - Nanya Technology (related party) NT$7,042,085 thousand, 71% of 2025 net sales (76% in 2024, 77% in Q1 2026); the company provides one-stop chip probing, assembly, final test and module services.

players.product: DRAM IC packaging and testing (wafer probe, assembly, final test) and DRAM memory module (DIMM) assembly - turn-key memory back-end OEM services

quarterly_data.quarter: Formosa Advanced Technologies annual report: 2025 Annual Report (06-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Letter to shareholders: in H2 2025 the major DRAM makers gave priority capacity to high-value HBM and DDR5 for AI demand, causing a structural DDR4 shortage from H2; Taiwanese DRAM fabs expanded DDR4 orders and output, lifting demand for downstream packaging and testing, and the company won DDR4 packaging/test orders and expanded bottleneck capacity. The company expects 2026 memory demand to keep exceeding supply and is cautiously optimistic on OEM packaging/test demand

quarterly_data.quarter: Formosa Advanced Technologies annual report: 2025 Annual Report (06-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: 2026 operating plan: raise DDR4 packaging/test order intake and capacity; develop advanced packaging processes and build lines for customers' high-speed DDR5 and customised memory; win more multi-chip, logic and Flash packaging customers; pursue DDR4 server memory module OEM orders and co-develop DDR5 server modules; add SMT lines to expand DDR5 gaming and standard module capacity

quarterly_data.quarter: Formosa Advanced Technologies annual report: 2025 Annual Report (06-10-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: New Factory 5 expansion for customers' long-term orders: construction began in 2022 and the use permit was obtained in 2025; cleanroom and utility systems are being built, with trial production and verification from H2 2026. The new plant will introduce TSV, bumping and high-speed test processes; wafer bumping and RDL lines are being set up, alongside development of 2- and 4-layer flip-chip stacking for AI and high-performance computing memory
